ui_bugs.issue: WebGL fallback is broken. When WebGL context is unavailable (getContext('webgl'|'webgl2') returns null), the three.js renderer throws a render-time error that propagates past the <Suspense fallback={SVGFallback}> wrapper and is caught by the top-level app error boundary, replacing the ENTIRE page with 'Something went wrong. Please refresh the page.' Suspense only catches lazy-loading promises, not render errors. The spec requires outcome cards to show legacy SVG diagrams in this scenario. Fix: wrap Scene3D (or the Outcome Scene wrapper) in a React ErrorBoundary that renders the SVG fallback on error, and/or detect WebGL support at mount time and short-circuit to SVG before mounting <Canvas>/<View>.

action_items: Add a React ErrorBoundary around the Scene3D/Three.js View in Outcome.jsx (and ideally in any other 3D-using component) that renders the SVG fallback on render error. Alternatively, do a cheap WebGL feature-detect (create a throwaway canvas, call getContext('webgl2')||getContext('webgl'); if null, set a context flag and render SVG directly). Suspense is insufficient because WebGL failures are synchronous render errors, not thrown promises.
critical_code_review_comments: Outcome.jsx uses <Suspense fallback={SVGFallback}>; this only handles the lazy chunk load path, not Three.js runtime errors. A dedicated ErrorBoundary is needed for graceful WebGL degradation.
The shared drei <View> design (single fixed canvas) means a single WebGL failure takes down ALL 3D-using sections simultaneously, amplifying the blast radius of the issue above.
